fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from the main driveway at first approach.
• Post a site map or structure diagram near the main entry point showing the location of both the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain vehicle clearance for emergency apparatus on both sides and overhead.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the rear of the property to open a secondary movement path for responders working around the back of the structures.
• Keep the rear access point unlocked or mark it with a visible indicator so responders can identify and use it without delay.
• Clear the equipment storage area of items that could block responder movement or staging along that side of the property.
• Keep the walkway and patio area clear of furniture, equipment, or stored items that could slow responder movement around the residence.
• Mark any ground-level hazards along the access drive or parking area, such as drainage edges or grade changes, so responders moving quickly in low-light conditions can see them.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim any shrubs that are growing directly next to the house or other structures.
• Thin scattered trees near structures so their branches do not touch or nearly touch each other.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the house clear of dry or dead plant material.
• Separate shrub groupings from structures by maintaining open ground between them.
• Remove dead branches from scattered trees near the house.
• Keep irrigated landscape plantings trimmed back from direct contact with exterior walls.
• Maintain open sight lines around structures by keeping shrubs low and well-spaced.
